statement: In December 2019, Rowling tweeted support for Maya Forstater.
Maya Forstater was a tax specialist.
Forstater lost her job because of tweets deemed transphobic.
Forstater brought an employment tribunal case.
She asked the tribunal whether the belief that sex is biologically determined was legally protected.
Judge Tayler ruled that this belief was not protected.
Rowling had become interested in transgender issues almost two years before the Forstater case.
Rowling had been following debates concerning gender identity during that period.
Rowling had met transgender people before writing the essay.
Rowling had read material by transgender people.
She had read material by gender specialists.
She had read material by intersex people.
She had read material by psychologists.
She had read material by safeguarding experts.
She had read material by social workers.
She had read material by doctors.
Her research was partly connected to writing her contemporary crime series.
Her fictional female detective is of an age where these issues would affect or interest her.
Trans activists had directed accusations and threats at Rowling on Twitter before the Forstater controversy.
The initial controversy surrounding Rowling's position began with a Twitter “like.”
Rowling had been screenshotting gender-related tweets/comments for later research.
The controversial “like” was accidental.
Rowling subsequently experienced persistent low-level harassment.
Rowling later followed Magdalen Berns on Twitter.
Berns was a feminist.
Berns was a lesbian.
Berns had an aggressive brain tumour.
Berns was dying when Rowling followed her.
Rowling followed Berns specifically because she wanted to contact her privately.
Rowling successfully contacted Berns.
Berns believed biological sex was important.
Berns argued that lesbians should not be considered bigoted for refusing sexual/romantic relationships with trans women who have penises.
Abuse directed at Rowling increased after she followed Berns.
Before publicly supporting Forstater, Rowling expected threats of violence.
Rowling subsequently received threats of violence.
People told Rowling that her statements were literally killing transgender people.
Rowling was called misogynistic/sexual slurs.
People burned copies of Rowling's books.
A man told Rowling that he had composted her books.
Rowling received a large number of emails and letters after publicly supporting Forstater.
The overwhelming majority were positive/supportive.
Some correspondents worked professionally with gender dysphoria/transgender people.
Correspondents expressed concerns about gender-identity politics influencing politics.
They expressed concerns about its influence on medical practice.
They expressed concerns about safeguarding.
They expressed concerns about risks to young people.
They expressed concerns about risks to gay people.
They expressed concerns about erosion of women's/girls' rights.
They expressed concerns about a climate of fear surrounding the subject.
Rowling had substantially withdrawn from Twitter before the Forstater tweet.
One reason was concern about Twitter's effects on her mental health.
Rowling returned to Twitter partly to promote/share a free children's book during COVID-19.
After returning, she again received hostile responses concerning transgender issues.
“TERF” stands for “trans-exclusionary radical feminist.”
The term was coined by trans activists.
Many women described as TERFs have never been radical feminists.
Mothers concerned that gay children might transition because of homophobic bullying have been called TERFs.
Women objecting to Marks & Spencer's changing-room policies have been called TERFs.
Marks & Spencer permitted people identifying as women to use women's changing rooms.
Radical feminists generally include trans men within their feminist analysis on the basis of birth sex.
Accusations of transphobia/TERFism have caused people to avoid publicly discussing gender-critical positions.
Institutions and organisations have similarly avoided expressing such positions because of anticipated accusations of transphobia.
Rowling had a charitable trust focused on alleviating social deprivation in Scotland.
The trust particularly focused on women and children.
Her trust supported projects involving female prisoners.
Her trust supported survivors of domestic abuse.
Her trust supported survivors of sexual abuse.
Rowling funded medical research into multiple sclerosis.
Multiple sclerosis behaves differently in males and females.
Trans activism was seeking changes to the legal definition/status of sex.
Trans activism sought to replace sex with gender/gender identity in at least some legal contexts.
Such changes could affect causes funded by Rowling.
Rowling was formerly a teacher.
Rowling founded a children's charity.
Rowling had previously publicly defended freedom of speech.
Rowling had defended Donald Trump's freedom of speech.
There had been a large increase in young women seeking gender transition.
The number of people detransitioning had increased.
Some detransitioners regret transitioning.
Some detransitioners underwent irreversible physical changes.
Some transition-related interventions can permanently impair/remove fertility.
Some detransitioners report that same-sex attraction contributed to their decision to transition.
Some detransitioners report that societal homophobia contributed to transitioning.
Some report that familial homophobia contributed to transitioning.
Around 2010, most people seeking transition were male.
By 2020, that sex ratio had reversed.
The UK experienced a 4,400% increase in girls referred for gender-transition-related treatment.
Autistic girls were substantially overrepresented among those referrals.
A comparable change in adolescent transgender identification occurred in the United States.
Lisa Littman was an American physician and researcher.
Littman published research concerning adolescent transgender identification in 2018.
Parents reported multiple members of friend groups identifying as transgender around the same period.
Littman investigated social contagion as a possible explanation.
Littman investigated peer influence as a possible factor.
Littman identified Tumblr as a possible contributing environment.
She identified Reddit.
She identified Instagram.
She identified YouTube.
Littman proposed/used the concept “rapid-onset gender dysphoria” (ROGD).
Littman characterized some online transgender youth communities as “insular echo chambers.”
Littman's paper generated substantial controversy.
Littman was accused of bias.
Littman was accused of spreading misinformation about transgender people.
Littman experienced significant personal abuse following publication.
There was an organized campaign to discredit Littman's research.
The journal removed/took offline Littman's paper.
The journal subsequently re-reviewed the paper.
The paper was subsequently republished.
Littman's career was adversely affected by the controversy.
Trans activists generally maintained that gender identity is innate.
Trans activists compared gender identity's innateness to sexual orientation.
Trans activists maintained that people could not be socially persuaded into becoming transgender.
Trans activists have argued that preventing a gender-dysphoric teenager from transitioning increases the likelihood of suicide.
Some activists specifically present transition as necessary to prevent suicide.
Marcus Evans was a psychiatrist.
Evans worked at the Tavistock gender clinic.
The Tavistock was an NHS gender clinic in England.
Evans resigned from the Tavistock.
Evans publicly criticized claims that children would kill themselves if prevented from transitioning.
Evans said such claims were not substantially supported by robust data/studies.
Evans said such claims did not align with cases encountered during his psychotherapy career.
Evans had worked as a psychotherapist for decades.
Rowling had severe OCD as a teenager.
Rowling's father openly stated that he would have preferred a son.
Rowling experienced significant ambivalence about being female when young.
Rowling experienced sexualised scrutiny/judgment as a girl/young woman.
Books and music were important coping mechanisms for Rowling's adolescent mental-health difficulties.
Transition is an effective/appropriate solution for at least some people with gender dysphoria.
Studies available by 2020 had found that 60–90% of gender-dysphoric teenagers eventually ceased experiencing gender dysphoria.
Multiple studies had consistently produced results in that approximate range.
Rowling personally knew several transgender people.
Rowling knew an older transsexual woman.
That woman had previously lived as a gay man.
That woman underwent an extensive evaluation process before transitioning.
That process included psychotherapy.
That process involved staged transition.
Historical sex-reassignment pathways generally required more extensive assessment than those available in 2020.
Trans activists were campaigning to remove/reduce those assessment requirements.
By 2020, a person could obtain a Gender Recognition Certificate without undergoing sex-reassignment surgery.
A person could obtain a GRC without taking cross-sex hormones.
A male person with neither surgery nor hormone treatment could legally become female under the UK's GRC framework.
Online pornography had become substantially more prevalent/accessible compared with the 1980s.
Online pornography contributes to harmful conditions experienced by girls.
Feminism had experienced a significant backlash.
Donald Trump had faced numerous sexual-assault allegations.
Trump had been recorded saying “grab them by the pussy.”
An organized/identifiable incel movement existed.
Incel communities expressed hostility toward women who refuse them sex.
Trans activists had publicly advocated punching TERFs.
Trans activists had advocated “re-educating” TERFs.
Some contemporary gender theories deny that femaleness resides in the sexed body.
Some advocates argue that biological women do not share meaningful/common sex-based experiences.
Some activists seek to diminish the political/legal significance of biological sex.
Some activists reject women as a coherent sex-based political class.
Rowling received hundreds of emails expressing concern about these developments.
Some trans activists maintain there is no materially relevant difference between trans women and natal women.
Institutions/activists were using terms such as “menstruators” instead of “women” in some contexts.
Institutions/activists were using “people with vulvas” in some contexts.
These linguistic changes were intended, at least partly, to include transgender/nonbinary people.
Some women regarded such terminology as dehumanising.
Some women regarded it as demeaning.
Some women regarded it as hostile or alienating.
Rowling is a survivor of domestic abuse.
Rowling is a survivor of sexual assault.
She had not publicly disclosed those experiences before 2020.
Her daughter from her first marriage shared part of the history surrounding Rowling's abusive marriage.
Rowling consulted her daughter before publicly discussing that history.
Her daughter encouraged her to disclose it.
Rowling's first marriage was violent.
Rowling had difficulty escaping that marriage.
Rowling subsequently married again.
Rowling continued to experience trauma-related reactions associated with past violence.
Rowling had a pronounced startle response/jumpiness.
Rowling experienced a serious sexual assault in her twenties.
The perpetrator was male.
Rowling believed the perpetrator exploited her situational vulnerability.
Transgender people experience elevated vulnerability to violence.
The majority of transgender people pose no threat to other people.
Transgender people are disproportionately vulnerable in some respects.
Transgender people are most likely to be killed by sexual/intimate partners.
Trans women working in the sex industry face particularly high risks of violence.
Trans women of colour face particularly high risks.
Male violence is an important source of lethal violence against trans women.
Allowing trans women into women's bathrooms can allow predatory non-trans men to exploit the same access policy.
Allowing trans women into women's changing rooms can create the same potential loophole.
Under some gender-identity policies, access to women's facilities requires no surgery.
Under some such policies, access requires no hormone treatment.
Self-identification policies permit male people to enter female-only spaces based principally/solely on declared gender identity.
Such policies make natal women/girls less safe.
Predatory men have exploited transgender-inclusive access rules or gender identities to access female spaces.
In June 2020, the Scottish government was proceeding with plans to reform gender recognition.
Those plans were controversial.
The reforms substantially reduced requirements for obtaining legal gender recognition.
The proposed system amounted to gender self-identification.
Under the proposed Scottish system, surgery would not be required.
Hormone treatment would not be required.
A medical diagnosis of gender dysphoria would not be required.
Rowling learned/read about the government's plans immediately before the Twitter incident described in the essay.
The news triggered memories of Rowling's sexual assault.
Rowling's controversial June 2020 tweets followed that episode.
Rowling received transphobia accusations after emphasizing biological sex.
She was called “cunt.”
She was called “bitch.”
She was called “TERF.”
People said Rowling deserved to be punched.
Rowling received death threats/wishes.
At least one person compared Rowling to Voldemort.
Trans activists had repeatedly targeted Rowling on social media before this incident.
Rowling believes “trans rights are human rights.”
Rowling believes “trans lives matter.”
Rowling believes transgender people deserve legal/social protection.
Rowling believes trans women should be protected from male violence.
Rowling expresses solidarity with trans women who experience domestic/sexual violence.
Rowling believes most transgender people pose no danger to others.
Rowling accepts that transition is appropriate for some gender-dysphoric people.
Rowling does not advocate eliminating transition altogether.
Rowling believes biological sex remains materially important.
Rowling believes “woman” should remain a biological/sex-based category.
Rowling opposes replacing sex with gender identity in at least some legal contexts.
Rowling supports retaining some female-only spaces.
Rowling believes safeguarding concerns can justify excluding trans women from some female-only spaces.
Rowling believes contemporary trans activism can harm women and girls.
Rowling believes contemporary trans activism can harm gay children.
Rowling believes contemporary trans activism can harm gender-dysphoric teenagers.
Rowling believes some trans activism provides cover/opportunities for male sexual predators.
Rowling supports freedom to express gender-critical beliefs.
Rowling identifies herself as standing alongside some transgender gender-critical people.
Large numbers of women were afraid of trans activists.
Women contacted Rowling reporting fear of doxxing.
Women reported fearing loss of employment.
Women reported fearing loss of livelihood.
Women reported fearing violence.
Women advocating female-only spaces had been characterized as bigots.
Polling showed majority support among women for Rowling's/general gender-critical concerns regarding single-sex spaces.
Women without personal experience of male violence/sexual assault were disproportionately likely to disagree with those concerns.
Gender-critical activism in Britain crossed traditional political-party lines.
Gender-critical women from different political affiliations were organizing together.
Those women shared concerns about erosion of women's existing rights.
Those women shared concerns about intimidation.
Rowling had personally spoken with multiple gender-critical women.
None of the gender-critical women Rowling had spoken with hated transgender people.
Many became involved because of concern about transgender youth.
Many were sympathetic toward transgender adults.
Some transgender adults opposed the form of trans activism Rowling criticized.
Transgender adults experienced backlash resulting from activism they did not personally endorse.
Use of “TERF” as a silencing/derogatory label contributed to increased interest in radical feminism among young women.
Radical feminism had experienced increased interest among young women around this period.
